 BOZEMAN, Mont. — The Montana State football team is fresh off a 56-20 win over Eastern Washington (2-6, 1-4) last Saturday and now will look to make it two in a row against Weber State (5-3, 4-1).
 The series history between these two programs leans in Montana State’s favor, 15-7, including five-straight wins. Last season was the highest margin of victory in series history, with MSU winning 66-14.
 This is Montana State’s first game back in Bobcat Stadium since their win over NAU on September 26, four weeks since their last home game.
 Weber State currently shares the lead with NAU of the Big Sky at 4-1 in conference play. The Wildcats are led by first-time collegiate head coach Eric Kjar and have already surprised their win total from the previous two seasons.
 The Wildcats have lost to Southern Utah, FBS Colorado and Portland State this season and have defeated Northern Colorado, Northwestern State, Cal Poly, Idaho and Idaho State.
 “I think (they are) a very changed team, (a) changed program,” Montana State head football coach Brent Vigen said of Weber State. “What Coach Kjar has been able to do there in a short time is get them back on track. They were certainly at the top of the league when I got here not too long ago, and they had fallen off. But he's got them back on track, and they're finding ways to win games.”
 Freshman quarterback Nate Dahle took over for Devin Brown in week two and has 1,591 passing yards this season and 17 total touchdowns to 10 interceptions.
 Weber’s leading receiver is junior Noah Kjar who has 47 receptions for 711 yards and 10 touchdowns.
 Their leading rusher is Spencer Ferguson with 72 carries for 543 yards and seven touchdowns. He missed two games this season, but rushed for 133 yards and a touchdown last week against Idaho State.
 Sophomore linebacker Teni Worthen leads the Wildcats in tackles this season with 36. He has also added one sack and two forced fumbles.
 The WSU defense leads the Big Sky in sacks this season and is one of the areas that Vigen spoke about in his Monday press conference.
 “They give you a lot of different looks,” Vigen said. “They are fairly aggressive at the same time, so they're willing to zero pressure you. So you know, bring in six or seven at times, bring five quite a bit, and then the D-line I do think is full of a bunch of really good players, and they play quite a few, so they stay fresh. They are willing to be very aggressive coverage wise, which allows you to be very aggressive pressure wise.”
 On the injury front, MSU wide receiver Taco Dowler's status is still questionable for Saturday's contest.
 Montana State will look to move to 7-1 overall and 4-1 in conference play on Saturday at 1 p.m. at Bobcat Stadium against Weber State.
